title: The Node runtime: V8, event loop and task queue

videos.script:
In the JavaScript course you met the event loop. One call stack, a queue of tasks, and a queue of microtasks emptied after each one. All of that is still true. {{pieces}} Today you open Node up and see what is underneath it: V8, which runs your code, and libuv, which gives Node its loop and a pool of threads.

{{phases}} The loop in Node is not one queue but several, visited in a fixed order. That order decides which of two ready callbacks runs first. You will see it decide, and you will see the one case where it does not.

{{pool}} Then the thread pool. Hash a password six times at once and watch four finish together and two wait. And then a hundred network requests at once, which add no threads at all.

{{block}} Then you break a server on purpose. One route that computes for two seconds, and one that does nothing. The one that does nothing takes two seconds too. You will measure it from outside, with curl, and from inside, with the loop's own delay.

{{end}} Last, how a process decides it is finished, and what happens to an error nobody caught. Both end a server, and only one of them on purpose.
